items.headline: AI-infrastructure selloff deepens: CoreWeave fell 15% and Oracle nearly 9% in one session, with both companies' bonds sold to record-high yields
items.why: The stress is in the debt financing the AI build-out, not just in equity valuations, which makes higher rates a direct threat to data-center spending.

sources.title: Nasdaq futures fall 1% as AI rout deepens on debt concerns

items.headline: TSMC posts a sixth straight record quarterly profit but guides cautiously on 2027 citing macro uncertainty
items.why: When the foundry at the center of AI chip supply hedges its outlook despite record earnings, it signals the market's growth assumptions are running ahead of the supplier's own.

sources.title: Nasdaq futures fall 1% as AI rout deepens on debt concerns

items.headline: South Korea's Kospi closes down 7.5% at 5,554 as SK Hynix falls 11% and Samsung Electronics 9.5%
items.why: Memory makers are the most leveraged public proxy for AI hardware demand, and both report Q3 results on October 28-29, so the volatility has a scheduled next test.

items.headline: Bitcoin drops below $81,000 and ether falls 6.5% to $2,353 as roughly $951 million of crypto positions are liquidated, $876 million of them longs
items.why: A leverage flush this large means the move was forced selling into a risk-off tape, and the open question is whether spot demand returns once the leverage is gone.

items.headline: US spot bitcoin ETFs record $150.5 million of outflows on October 14, reversing a $175.7 million inflow the day before
items.why: Institutional demand is flipping day to day with the macro tape rather than providing a steady bid.

items.headline: Strategy bought another 250 BTC at an average of about $86,194, lifting holdings to 848,250 BTC against an average cost near $75,444
items.why: The largest corporate holder is still adding but at prices well above its average cost, so its position stays profitable only while bitcoin holds above the mid-$70,000s.

items.headline: US September CPI runs hotter than forecast: 3.7% year over year (3.6% expected) with core at 2.6% (2.5% expected)
items.why: Core inflation accelerating alongside an energy shock is what moves the Fed from holding to hiking.

items.headline: US producer prices jump 1.3% in September, the largest monthly gain since March 2022, and are up 6.3% from a year earlier
items.why: Producer costs lead consumer prices, so this raises the odds that the CPI pressure spreads beyond energy in the coming months.

items.headline: Fed hike odds reprice: about 37% for the October 27-28 meeting and about 91% for at least one hike by December
items.why: The December meeting is now the live decision, and rate-sensitive assets are trading off that date rather than October.

items.headline: A tanker is sunk in the Strait of Hormuz, yet Brent slips about 2% to near $103.7 on the day
items.why: Shipping attacks in the strait are keeping oil near $100 and feeding the inflation prints, while the muted price reaction suggests the risk is already largely priced.

items.headline: Gold falls nearly 2% to $4,073.73 an ounce, its lowest since early October, and silver drops 4.1% to $56.99
items.why: Gold is trading as a rates-and-dollar instrument right now: higher hike odds and a firmer dollar are outweighing the geopolitical bid.

items.why: Oil near $100 is the input behind the hot inflation data, so it is the commodity that decides the rate path.

items.why: A long run of calm ended on a single macro print, which resets how much downside the market had been pricing.

items.why: Leadership is narrowing: the damage is concentrated in AI and semiconductors while healthcare and staples rise. These are intraday levels, not closes.

items.why: The chip sector's losing streak and a 10-year yield above 5% are the two levels the equity rally has to contend with.
